title: Finite assembly, source-basis cost reduction, and E8 verification
body:
Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave an avoidable gap below the retained balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a **constructive finite-assembly theorem and exact verifier** that reach every rational target strictly below that ceiling. The source-basis, contract-checking and E8 verification contributions listed below remain included.

### Focused theorem and review boundary

For admitted rational bit and complex caps `c,b`, let `a0 = 384599/10^10` and `u = min(b,c)`. Assuming `a0 < u`, `b < 1/32`, an admitted finite coefficient charge, and the inherited weighted-bootstrap and bridge interfaces, every rational

```text
0 < kappa < u/(1+u)
```

has a constructible finite witness. The constructor chooses positive backoffs, finitely many bootstrap levels and explicit integer cutoffs, then checks all **47 retained strict inequalities**. The proof establishes termination and exact maximality on a supplied rational grid, relative to these caps and this assembly family. The ceiling itself is not attained.

Start with the [review entry](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e819106ee098953be69cdac9aff47bdece567bc4/research/finite-assembly-frontier/README.md), [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e819106ee098953be69cdac9aff47bdece567bc4/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md), and [constructor](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/e819106ee098953be69cdac9aff47bdece567bc4/research/finite-assembly-frontier/assembly.py). The package is self-contained for default offline verification and can be reviewed independently of the other E8 packages. Retain **all 50 manifested files plus MANIFEST.json**, including original source pins, notices, supplier receipts, logs and the finite invoice.

The worked example pins [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433) at `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`. On a `10^-27` grid it gives

```text
kappa = 280216238064569651155257 / 250000000000000000000000000
      = 0.001120864952258278604621028
```

This exceeds that historical baseline by approximately `6.04621e-19`. The reusable parameter theorem and verifier are the contribution; this example makes no current numerical-lead, new-supplier or practical-speedup claim.

Different caps require their own source-bound admission, full finite invoice and a match to the bootstrap/bridge premises. The default 512-bit coefficient charge is justified for the retained example. The historical moment adapter charges both suppliers' bad-residue envelope; [PR559](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/559) removes that surcharge on the native complex side while retaining it on the bit side. An appropriate cap-admission adapter is required before replacing the historical inputs. Changing CLI values alone does not establish those premises.

### Validation

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Python 3.11+ and the standard library suffice, with assertions enabled. Add `--output /absolute/path/to/new-result.json` to retain every exact parameter, cutoff and margin.

The verifier checks package closure, public source/Git hashes, retained supplier receipts and their cross-references, and the complete finite invoice. It recomputes both supplier moments and the selected seed with two rational engines, reproduces the baseline assembly, and verifies nine finite bootstrap levels and all 47 inequalities. The next grid point, zero eta, zero beta and unit beta are rejected. Five behavioral tests cover 48 cap/target regimes, strict endpoints, zero-step cases, invalid premises and 100-digit-grid JSON output.

The original pinned supplier replay passed all 13 stages in 6.19 seconds and reused its source-bound Gaussian phase evidence. Default package verification reuses those retained receipts; it does not repeat the supplier word, geometry or phase computations.

The focused entry update changes **only README.md and its manifest hash**. The other 49 manifested files are byte-identical. Ody independently reviewed the updated claims and reran the default verifier on Python 3.14.8: five tests, nine finite levels and all 47 inequalities passed. Root audited the receipt and all 51 before/after file bindings; no package file changed during verification. Manifest: `7ad89943890fb6b206fa3b769d16b77f66d0e4a2d9009abb6ff5e2116252a23c`.

Current head: [`e819106`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/e819106ee098953be69cdac9aff47bdece567bc4). All **60 jobs across five fork push workflows passed on this exact commit**: [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38317707790), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38317707807), [recycled registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38317708003), [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38317707865), and [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38317707841). Verified October 13, 2026. These are fork CI results; upstream maintainer review remains separate.

Historical exact-head validation: signed, GitHub-verified [`a65780b`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/a65780b0d5664c33da16e704de4d6f228a7b816b) passed all 60 jobs across five workflows: [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135907), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203136057), [recycled registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135954), [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135904), and [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135946). Those results apply to that earlier head.

### Scope and attribution

Supplier compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. This PR does not establish an unconditional multiplication theorem, global optimality or a new Lean proof. The separate unpublished prototype is not part of this submission.

Contributed by George Lydakis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody's independent review. Original notices, licenses, source pins and earlier attribution are preserved. PR447/PR438 retain rohanarun's credits; PR442 retains DaysSky's credits and Claude attribution; the kernel method retains Chafik Boukhalfa's attribution. PR433 remains credited to icekylinx with OpenAI Codex and its upstream contributors Zhihao Chen, ai-nanachi, Dylan Crow and Jacob Sussman. The unchanged outer engine retains eumemic/Anthropic Claude, icekylinx, Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures credits. Full package notices remain authoritative.
